slot.topic_title: Scalars and Vectors in One Dimension

item.title: Distance, Displacement, and Speed of a Hallway Robot
item.stimulus:
A delivery robot moves along a straight east–west hallway. Take east as the positive direction. Starting from its charging station, the robot makes three trips in order. During each trip it moves in only one direction.

Trip | Direction | Distance moved (m)
1 | east | 12
2 | west | 20
3 | east | 5

A second robot, Robot B, starts at the same charging station and makes a single trip of 3 m west.

parts.prompt: Calculate the total distance traveled by the first robot during the three trips. Then calculate its displacement from the charging station at the end of trip 3, giving it as a signed value and stating its direction.

criteria.text: Total distance = 12 m + 20 m + 5 m = 37 m, found by adding the sizes of the three trips without regard to direction.
criteria.evidence: Response adds the three trip lengths as positive quantities and gets 37 m.
criteria.fix: Distance is a scalar: add the length of every trip as a positive number, ignoring direction.

criteria.text: Displacement = (+12 m) + (−20 m) + (+5 m) = −3 m, that is, 3 m west of the charging station.
criteria.evidence: Response gives east trips positive signs and the west trip a negative sign, sums them to −3 m, and states the direction is west.
criteria.fix: Displacement is a vector: give each trip a sign for its direction, add the signed values, then read direction from the sign.

parts.prompt: Explain why the first robot's displacement at the end of trip 3 is equal to Robot B's displacement, even though the first robot traveled a much greater distance.

criteria.text: Explains that displacement depends only on the net change in position, so both robots have −3 m (3 m west), while distance counts every meter traveled.
criteria.evidence: Response states both displacements are −3 m (3 m west) and explains why, either by signed trips canceling in the vector sum (−20 m against +17 m) or by both robots starting and ending at the same positions, and contrasts this with distance.
criteria.fix: Compare only start and end positions for displacement; distance adds every trip regardless of direction.

parts.prompt: During trip 2, the robot's velocity component is v_x = −0.80 m/s. A student states that the robot's speed during trip 2 is −0.80 m/s. Explain what is wrong with the student's statement, and give the robot's correct speed during trip 2.

criteria.text: States that the speed is 0.80 m/s, because speed is a scalar equal to the magnitude of the velocity and is never negative.
criteria.evidence: Response gives the speed as 0.80 m/s (positive) and identifies speed as a scalar or as the magnitude of velocity.
criteria.fix: Speed is a scalar: report the size of the velocity only, as a positive number, and drop the sign.

criteria.text: Explains that the negative sign in v_x = −0.80 m/s is direction information: the velocity, a vector, points west (the negative direction).
criteria.evidence: Response states that the minus sign shows the velocity is directed west, opposite to the chosen positive direction, and that speed does not carry direction.
criteria.fix: In one dimension, read the sign of a vector component as its direction; negative here means west.

item.model_answer:
(a) Total distance = 12 m + 20 m + 5 m = 37 m. Distance is a scalar, so each trip adds its length regardless of direction.
Displacement = (+12 m) + (−20 m) + (+5 m) = −3 m. The first robot ends 3 m west of the charging station.

(b) Displacement is a vector, so in the sum the eastward trips (+12 m and +5 m, total +17 m) and the westward trip (−20 m) have opposite signs and mostly cancel, leaving a net change in position of −3 m. Robot B's single trip also gives a displacement of −3 m, so the two displacements are equal (3 m west). Distance is a scalar, so for the first robot nothing cancels and it is 37 m, compared with 3 m for Robot B.

(c) Speed is a scalar equal to the magnitude of the velocity, so it cannot be negative. The robot's speed during trip 2 is 0.80 m/s. The negative sign in v_x = −0.80 m/s tells the direction of the velocity vector: the robot is moving west, the negative direction.
item.verification_python:
trips=[12,-20,5]
dist=sum(abs(t) for t in trips)
assert dist==37
disp=sum(trips)
assert disp==-3
robotB=-3
assert disp==robotB
assert 12+5==17
vx=-0.80
speed=abs(vx)
assert abs(speed-0.80)<1e-12
assert vx<0
print('ALL_CHECKS_PASSED')
